Subject: Quick ask — 3-week runway or equivalent credit for our POC

Hi Kimberly,

Thanks again for the smooth onboarding — the Redwood trial has been great and our ML team is seeing consistent gains. We have one hiccup: our product spike next week will use more tokens than we expected and our 30-day POC will hit the cap on Aug 24.

Two asks from my side: can we either (A) extend the POC by 3 weeks (same access, no extra seats) or (B) give us a one-off token credit equivalent to roughly 3 weeks of expected usage (~1.2M tokens)? Procurement is flexible but wants a clear amendment for audit.

Also, can you confirm whether the extended time would be covered by the current pilot SLA and if there would be any extra charges if we pass the spike? We might be ready to convert earlier if we see production parity, so any conversion incentives would help.

Would appreciate an outline of options and costs.

Best,
Erin

Hi Erin — great to hear the trial is progressing. Short answer: yes, we can do either path (time extension or token credit). I outlined two pragmatic paths below so procurement can pick: 

Option 1 — 3-week extension (no change to seats or routes)
- No incremental monthly fee; we extend the current POC window to Sep 14.
- SLA: same pilot SLA applies (uptime and basic incident SLAs).
- Usage beyond the current agreed cap during the extended window would be billed at standard PAYG rates unless you opt into a top-up credit.

Option 2 — Token credit (~1.2M tokens)
- We issue a one-time token credit applied to the account (expires 90 days from issuance).
- If you hit the credit, you can either: (a) convert to a commit for a discount, or (b) pay PAYG for overage.

Conversion incentive we can attach: if Sentrylane signs a 6-month dedicated/commit contract by Oct 1, we can offer a conversion credit equal to 25% of the credit value (applies toward first invoice).

I put together a short addendum draft and attached a redline for procurement (POC_Addendum_Sentrylane_v1.pdf). If you want, I can run a one-time concession by our Sales Manager for a slightly larger credit.

Which option do you prefer? Happy to hop on a 15-min call to walk through numbers.

Thanks,
Kimberly Park

Erin — thanks for the questions. Answers below and next steps at the bottom.

1) SLA / routing: The extension keeps the same pilot SLA (availability/incident priority). For latency-sensitive routing we can keep your priority tag on the trial routes for the extended window; I noted this in the addendum. If you start sustained high-volume usage beyond the cap we may throttle to maintain fairness across trials — we'll always notify 24 hours in advance for any throttling events.

2) Credit application: We can apply one-time credits at the project level. Please send the project IDs for dev/staging and we'll stitch the credit accordingly. Credits expire 90 days after issuance.

3) Conversion incentive math (example):
- Token credit value offered: $6,000 (equivalent to ~1.2M tokens at PAYG).
- If Sentrylane signs a 6-month commit by 2026-10-01 we will apply 25% of $6,000 = $1,500 as a credit on the first invoice.
- Fallback: if no commit by 10/01, credit remains $6,000 but no additional conversion credit; we can offer 15% conversion credit as a manager-approved option if procurement agrees to net-30 billing terms (conditional approval).

Attached: SOC2_summary_link.txt (link to exec summary) and the unsigned addendum (POC_Addendum_Sentrylane_v1.pdf). I also dropped the DocuSign URL for the amendment here: https://app.redwood.ai/docusign/SL-2026-087-amendment

Next steps:
- Erin: confirm preferred path (extension vs token credit) and share project IDs and procurement contact for the addendum.
- Procurement: if you want the manager-approved 15% fallback instead of straight 25%/0% split, say so and Ben will finalize pricing language.
- We can also schedule a 15-min call Monday to finalize.

Thanks — I can send the signed amendment template as soon as you confirm project IDs.

Kim
